mainTopic: A deathbed gift (מתנת שכיב מרע) that also records a קנין: the dispute between רב and שמואל, the contradictions in each one's rulings and how they are resolved, and רבא's challenge to שמואל
overview: The גמרא brings a dispute about a שכיב מרע (a person on his deathbed) whose gift document also records a קנין (a formal act of acquisition). רב's study hall says this gift is doubly strong. Like a healthy person's gift, it cannot be taken back if he recovers. Like a deathbed gift, it can even transfer a loan by words alone. שמואל is unsure, because maybe the giver meant the gift to work only through the שטר, and a שטר cannot take effect after death. The גמרא then sets each אמורא against himself. In the 'write and give a מנה' case, רב worries about the document problem and שמואל does not. The answer for רב is that his two rulings differ on whether a קנין was done. The answer for שמואל is that in the 'write and give' case the document only adds strength for the recipient. Finally רבא challenges שמואל with another of his rulings: a dying man who gave away everything, even with a קנין, can take it back if he recovers. The challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute: a deathbed gift that also records a formal acquisition
steps.stepSummary: רב's study hall says the giver gave the recipient 'two horses to ride' (double strength). שמואל says he does not know how to rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: a deathbed gift whose document says a קנין was also done. רב's study hall says in רב's name: he put him on two horses. שמואל said: I don't know how to rule about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new dispute between רב and שמואל about a deathbed gift whose document records that a קנין was also made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deathbed gift normally works by words alone, and a healthy person's gift needs a קנין. Here the dying man did both. רב sees this as doubly strong. שמואל has a doubt, which the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated: introduces a dispute between אמוראים
A gift given by a person on his deathbed
A formal act that transfers ownership
He put him on two horses: the gift is strengthened in two ways
I don't know what to rule about it

phrases.english: It was stated: a gift of a person on his deathbed
in which it is written that a קנין was done
The study hall of רב say in the name of רב:
He mounted him on two horses.
phrases.notes: A picture: the recipient now holds the gift in two strong ways at once.

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
I do not know what to rule about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: מַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע שֶׁכָּתוּב בָּהּ קִנְיָן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: the gift is doubly strong. שמואל: he is unsure whether it is valid.

steps.title: What 'two horses' means: the strengths of both kinds of gift
steps.stepSummary: רב's view is explained. The gift is like a healthy person's gift, so he cannot take it back if he recovers. It is also like a deathbed gift, so even a loan owed to him passes by his words alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a healthy man's gift, because if he gets better he cannot take it back. It is like a dying man's gift, because if he said 'the loan owed to me goes to so-and-so,' that person gets the loan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב's phrase and explains which two advantages the recipient gets.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a dying man's gift can be cancelled if he recovers. Because of the קנין, this one cannot. Normally a healthy person cannot transfer a debt owed to him by words alone. Because this is still a deathbed gift, his words do transfer the loan.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift of a healthy person
He recovered (literally, 'stood up')
He cannot take it back
His loan: money others owe him

phrases.english: The study hall of רב say in the name of רב:
He mounted him on two horses:
it is like a gift of a healthy person,
and it is like a gift of a person on his deathbed.
It is like a gift of a healthy person:
if he recovers, he cannot retract.
It is like a gift of a person on his deathbed:
if he said, 'his loan is to so-and-so,'
his loan belongs to so-and-so.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַתְּנַת בָּרִיא, הֲרֵי הִיא כְּמַתְּנַת שְׁכִיב מְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רב's short phrase from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gift cannot be taken back if he recovers, and it can still transfer a loan by words alone.

steps.title: Why שמואל is unsure: maybe he meant to give only through the document
steps.stepSummary: שמואל fears that writing a קנין shows the giver wanted the gift to take effect only through the שטר. A שטר cannot take effect after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: I don't know how to rule. Perhaps he decided to give it only through a document, and a document does not work after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reason behind שמואל's doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A deathbed gift takes effect only at death. If the giver relied on the שטר, the transfer would have to happen through the שטר after he died, and that cannot work. So the extra קנין might actually weaken the gift.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps he did not fully decide to transfer it (except in this way)
A written document or deed
A document does not take effect after the giver's death

steps.whatToRemember: רב sees the קנין as making the gift stronger. שמואל fears it shows the giver relied only on the שטר, which cannot work after death.

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
I do not know what to rule about it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא לֹא גָּמַר לְהַקְנוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטָר,
phrases.english: since perhaps he resolved to transfer it to him only with a document,
and there is no document after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא לֹא גָּמַר לְהַקְנוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives שמואל's side, in parallel to the explanation of רב in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The gift is in doubt, because perhaps he meant it to work only through a שטר, which cannot take effect after death.

steps.title: Contradiction: רב worries about the document problem elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets רב against himself, and שמואל against himself. Through רבי אלעזר, רב ruled that if a dying man said 'write and give a מנה' and then died, we do not write it, because perhaps he meant to give only through the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contrasted רב with רב, and שמואל with שמואל. רבין sent in the name of רבי אבהו: Know that רבי אלעזר sent to Babylonia in רב's name: a dying man said 'write and give a מנה to so-and-so,' and he died. We do not write and give, since perhaps he meant to transfer it only by the document, and a document does not work after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a double contradiction. In this step it brings רב's ruling from another case, where he uses the very worry that he brushed aside in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'write and give' case, רב worries that the giver relied only on the שטר. That is exactly שמואל's reasoning here. Yet with the written קנין, רב did not worry about this at all.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted רב's statement with another statement of רב
To the Diaspora, meaning Babylonia
Our teacher: here this means רב
Write and give: an instruction to write a document and deliver it
A sum of one hundred דינרים

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction between רב and רב,
and between שמואל and שמואל.
For רבין sent in the name of רבי אבהו:

phrases.aramaic: הֱווֹ יָדְעִי שֶׁשָּׁלַח רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לַגּוֹלָה
phrases.english: You should know that רבי אלעזר sent to the Diaspora
in the name of our teacher:
phrases.notes: 'Our teacher' here means רב, so this is רב's ruling.

phrases.english: A person on his deathbed who said:
'Write and give a מנה to so-and-so,'
and he died:
we do not write and give,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא לֹא גָּמַר לְהַקְנוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטָר,
phrases.english: since perhaps he resolved to transfer it to him only with a document,
and there is no document after death.

steps.confusionAlert: Watch who says what. In this case רב uses the 'maybe only through a document' worry, which in step 3 was שמואל's reasoning. That switch is the whole contradiction.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the consistency of רב's position from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a deathbed gift with a written קנין is doubly strong
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the 'write and give' case רב worries that the giver relied only on the שטר. Why doesn't he worry about the same thing when a קנין is written?

steps.title: The other half of the contradiction: שמואל says to write and give
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that in the 'write and give' case we do write and give. He does not worry that the giver meant only the document, even though that was his worry about the written קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in שמואל's name: the הלכה is that we write and give.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the double contradiction by showing that שמואל rules the opposite way from what his doubt in step 3 would suggest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 3 שמואל feared the gift rested only on the שטר. Here, in a similar case, he lets the gift go through without that fear. So each אמורא seems to hold the other's reasoning, and the גמרא will need to resolve this.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is
We write the document and give it to the recipient

steps.whatToRemember: In the 'write and give' case, רב worries about 'only through a document' and שמואל does not. That is the reverse of their positions on the written קנין, so both seem to contradict themselves.

phrases.english: And רב יהודה said that שמואל said:
The הלכה is: we write and give.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, הִלְכְתָא: כּוֹתְבִין וְנוֹתְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the contradiction announced in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's doubt about a deathbed gift with a written קנין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here שמואל does not worry that the giver relied only on the שטר. Why does he worry about it when a קנין is written?

steps.title: Summing up the two contradictions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that both רב and שמואל seem to contradict themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב's two rulings clash with each other, and שמואל's two rulings clash with each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the two contradictions it just laid out in steps 4 and 5 and states them plainly. This sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב gave the gift 'double strength' in the קנין case, yet in the 'write and give' case he worried the giver meant the document only. שמואל worried about the document in the קנין case, yet ordered the document written in the 'write and give' case. Each rabbi seems to flip his own logic.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a contradiction that needs an answer
רב's statement against רב's other statement

phrases.english: Rav's statement is difficult against Rav's other statement,
and Shmuel's statement is difficult against Shmuel's other statement!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא דְּרַב אַדְּרַב, קַשְׁיָא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אַדִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States outright the two contradictions built in steps 4 and 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רב and of שמואל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each rabbi seems to rule one way in the קנין case and the opposite way in the 'write and give' case.

steps.title: Answering רב: was a קנין done or not
steps.stepSummary: רב's two rulings deal with different cases. In one a קנין was done, and in the other it was not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב does not contradict himself. In the 'two horses' case they made a קנין with the giver. In the 'write and give' case there was no קנין, only words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction in רב by showing that his two rulings speak about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a קנין was done, the gift is strong enough to work even without the document, so רב gives it double strength. When the giver only said 'write and give' with no קנין, maybe he wanted the gift to work only through the document. A document cannot be written after death, so we do not write it.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a קנין (formal act of acquisition) with him
This case ... that case; a split between two situations

phrases.english: Rav against Rav is not difficult –
this is where they made an act of acquisition with him,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the 'two horses' ruling from step 1.

phrases.english: that is where they did not make an act of acquisition with him.
phrases.notes: 'That' is the 'write and give a מנה' case, where he only gave a spoken instruction.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַב אַדְּרַב לָא קַשְׁיָא – הָא דִּקְנוֹ מִינֵּיהּ, הָא דְּלָא קְנוֹ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): קנין versus no קנין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב seemed to give the gift full strength in one case but worry about the document in the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קנין makes the difference. With a קנין the gift stands on its own, and without one we worry he relied on the document.

steps.title: Answering שמואל: the document only strengthens the recipient
steps.stepSummary: In the 'write and give' case, the giver added the document only to make the recipient's hold stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל does not contradict himself. When he says to write and give, it is a case where the giver is only strengthening the recipient's position with a document.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction in שמואל by explaining what the document means in the 'write and give' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'write and give' case, the document is an extra benefit for the recipient. It is not a condition the gift depends on. So שמואל does not worry there that the gift works only through the document, and we write it even after death.

keyTerms.meaning: Strengthens his power; adds a document to give the recipient extra security

phrases.english: Shmuel against Shmuel is not difficult –
it is a case where he is strengthening his power.
phrases.notes: 'His power' means the recipient's. The document is a bonus for the recipient, not the thing the gift depends on.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אַדִּשְׁמוּאֵל לָא קַשְׁיָא – בִּמְיַפֶּה אֶת כֹּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the contradiction from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the document only strengthens the recipient
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל seemed to worry about the document in one case and ignore that worry in the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the document clearly only strengthens the recipient, there is no worry that the gift depends on it.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: a קנין makes the gift work by itself, and without a קנין we fear he relied on the document. שמואל: when the document only adds strength for the recipient, we write it even after death.

steps.title: רבא questions whether שמואל really holds the document worry
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן whether שמואל really said the giver may have meant the gift only through the document, citing another ruling of שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק sat behind רבא, and רבא sat before רב נחמן and asked him: Did שמואל really say, 'Maybe the giver meant to give only through the document, and a document does not work after death'? But רב יהודה said in שמואל's name: a dying man who wrote all his property to others, even if they made a קנין with him, can take it back if he gets better!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge opens. רבא brings a different ruling of שמואל that seems to clash with שמואל's worry about the document. The full point of the challenge continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's worry was that a קנין shows the giver wanted the gift through the document, like a healthy person's gift. But in this other ruling, even with a קנין, the giver can take it back if he recovers. That treats the gift as a deathbed gift, not as a healthy person's gift made through the document.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say? Opens a challenge to a reported view
But didn't he say? Brings a contradicting statement
A person on his deathbed
If he recovers, he takes the gift back

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the people: רב נחמן בר יצחק sits behind, while רבא asks the question to רב נחמן, a different רב נחמן sitting in front.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אֲחוֹרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak was sitting behind Rava,
and Rava was sitting before Rav Naḥman,
and he was asking him –
Did Shmuel really say:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא לֹא גָּמַר לְהַקְנוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטָר,
phrases.english: perhaps he resolved to transfer it to him only through the document,
and there is no document after death?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁכִיב מְרַע שֶׁכָּתַב כׇּל נְכָסָיו לַאֲחֵרִים,
phrases.english: a person on his deathbed who wrote all his property to others,
even though they made an act of acquisition with him –
if he recovered, he takes it back;

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: שֶׁמָּא לֹא גָּמַר לְהַקְנוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטָר, וְאֵין שְׁטָר לְאַחַר מִיתָה? וְהָא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the contradictions are settled, a new challenge against שמואל's position from step 3 begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's worry that a קנין shows the giver meant the gift only through the document
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a קנין made the gift work through the document like a healthy person's gift, he could not take it back on recovery. Yet שמואל rules elsewhere that even with a קנין he can take it back.
